attackVerdicts.attack: Bun autoloads repo .env/.env.local before loadEnvFiles, so the ADR-0555 provenance registry never sees those keys and R1's operatorEnvFrom filter is blind.
attackVerdicts.evidence: probe entry-dotenv.ts compiled with the build-cli flags, cwd holding a pre-existing .env (QUANTA_TRUSTED_PATHS=/forged/by/repo), .env.local and .env.dev. Output: before="/forged/by/repo", beforeLocal="L", prov=null, provLocal=null, provDev=<repo>/.env.dev. The same entry compiled with --no-compile-autoload-dotenv gives before=null and prov=<repo>/.env, provLocal=<repo>/.env.local. So once Bun autoload is off, loadEnvFiles (env-files.ts:47-64) is the only dotenv source and the registry is complete. Note that app-level loadEnvFiles still puts the forged value into process.env (after="/forged/by/repo") even with the flag. The filter is therefore necessary but only sufficient after A's flag. attackVerdicts.attack: TrustStore keys on normalize(), not realpath(), so realpath grants and symlinked or /tmp lookups disagree.
attackVerdicts.verdict: CONFIRMED (as an unpinned contract with fail-closed misses; REFUTED as a bypass)
attackVerdicts.evidence: trust-store.ts:48-70 documents the store as lexical by design: 'the host resolves symlinks via realpath BEFORE handing the path in'. The existing callers do realpath the cwd (apps/agent/index.ts:313-318, mcp-composition.ts:465-470, configured-endpoint-wire.ts:78-86), but they never realpath QUANTA_TRUSTED_PATHS entries (canonicalizeTrustedPaths, trust-store.ts:166-178). probe-trust-canon.ts: grant setTrusted(realpath) gives isTrusted(real)=true, isTrusted(lexical /tmp path)=false, isTrusted(symlink)=false, and envList[/tmp lexical].has(realpath(cwd))=false, envList[symlink].has(realpath(cwd))=false. loadRepoRules walks lexically: resolve(cwd), no realpath (repo-rules.ts:113-133). Every mismatch fails closed, which means a user's legitimate grant is silently missed, not a bypass. It is a live regression risk for a new gate on macOS, where os.tmpdir()=/var/folders is a symlink to /private/var. R1's resolveProjectTrust did take a realpath port, but the env-list side and the walk side were unspecified.

revisedDesign.summary: Two file-disjoint lanes. (B) BUG-1, ready now. messageSchema gains `origin`. The guarantee that no Message field is ever silently dropped is a runtime round-trip census: a fixture whose type, Complete<Message>, makes tsc require every optional key at every depth and every ContentBlock variant is pushed through an exhaustive Record of production persistence rails. A single Message-node type guard stays as a shallow value-domain early warning, honestly labeled. Consumers attribute speakers through the existing summaryRoleOf/isSyntheticUserMessage. (S) SEC-5 and its siblings. One ProjectTrustDecision is minted per surface composition root from operator-controlled inputs under a pinned realpath canonicalization and required by every repo-authority loader. Its forge resistance depends on cluster A disabling Bun's dotenv and bunfig autoload in the compiled binary; D consumes that invariant and does not re-land it.
revisedDesign.structuralMechanism: BUG-1: (1) a compile-complete fixture type in tests/_support/complete-message.ts. `Complete<T>` makes optional keys required recursively and maps an array of a `type`-discriminated union to a Record keyed by the discriminant. Adding any field or variant to Message, at any depth, breaks typecheck:tests (probe-complete-fixture.ts proves this at depth 3 and for a new variant). (2) `MESSAGE_RAILS: Record<MessageRailId, RailFn>` with a runtime drift guard (`Object.keys` === `MESSAGE_RAIL_IDS`). Each entry calls a production function, and each output must deep-equal the fixture, so a schema that strips any key at any depth goes RED. That is zod object stripping, the same mechanism measured for origin. (3) Single decode chokepoint: readSessionSnapshot is the only safeParse of savedSessionSchema, pinned by a syntax census. (4) A Message-node `__Eq<__Norm<z.output<typeof messageSchema>>, __Norm<Message>>` private const in saved-session-schema.ts. It is labeled as an early warning for value domains at depth ≤2 and not a completeness proof, because TS deep identity is order- and depth-limited. SEC-5: (5) `ProjectTrustDecision` is a discriminated union branded by a module-private unique symbol in src/config/project-trust.ts, minted only by `resolveProjectTrust` and `grantProjectTrust`. `TrustedProjectRoot` is the required parameter of loadRepoRules, readMcpConfig's projectRoot, loadNamedAgents, the project-grants overlay, vendor/glob rules, plugin auto-wire and legacy settings.json hooks. (6) `CanonicalProjectRoot` = canonicalizeProjectPath(realpath(git-root-of(realpath(cwd)) ?? realpath(cwd))). It is the TrustStore key, the rules-walk start and the walk bound; env-listed paths are realpath'd, and failures are dropped. (7) `MODE_PROJECT_TRUST_SOURCE: Record<AgentMode, 'operator-grant'|'host-attested'|'never'>` with a drift guard replaces the mode→load Record. (8) Operator env view = process.env minus keys attributed in envFileProvenance(), complete only because cluster A compiles with --no-compile-autoload-dotenv/--no-compile-autoload-bunfig. The trust store path must be absolute and must not canonicalize inside the decision root (containment check, defense in depth for source-mode runs). revisedDesign.compatibilityAndMigration: BUG-1 is additive. Legacy sessions without origin load unchanged and the id-prefix fallback stays. Already-rewritten sessions have lost origin permanently; reconstructing it from text would be a heuristic, so the loss is accepted. A V1 or portable file carrying a non-'harness' origin is now refused (fail-closed). SEC-5 changes behavior. A trusted folder behaves as today. An untrusted folder does not load repo-authority artifacts and shows a notice. About 12 existing positive-path tests must obtain real grants through resolveProjectTrust with in-memory persistence (cli-repo-rules-wire-hellgate, mode-preset-repo-rules-wire-hellgate, interactive-repo-rules e2e/wire, repo-rules*.test.ts, agents-md-scope-e2e, sota-codex-full, config-migration-persist*); the brand-cast census covers tests too. There is no dotenv-settable rollback switch (ADR-0470 posture: 'never an env var a hostile repo could also set', provenance-guard.ts:34-38). The TrustStore file format is unchanged; keys become realpath-canonical, which matches the existing hooks-flow writer (apps/agent/index.ts:313-363). Existing lexical-key records written by hand still match when the path has no symlinks. Coordinate with cluster A: D's operator-env view is only complete after A's build flags. Until then S3 must not be declared forge-resistant.
revisedDesign.userVisibleBehavior: BUG-1: resumed sessions keep harness attribution. The next compaction labels summaries [harness], memory distillation no longer files harness text as '### user', and /rewind (with message ids on) never offers a summary as a turn to undo. SEC-5 (after decisions): in a TTY, an untrusted folder that ships AGENTS.md, .mcp.json, agents, grants or plugins gets a one-time prompt listing them. y persists to ~/.quanta/trust.json keyed by the realpath git root. N continues without them, and /rules and /status show them as ignored. Non-TTY, CI, IDE and web show a one-line notice or readout banner naming the ignored files and the grant channels. A repo .env can no longer make a folder trusted or relocate the trust store; that also requires cluster A's build flags.
revisedDesign.rollout: BUG-1 is default-on immediately: it is a pure fidelity fix and nobody would want it off. The SEC-5 `.mcp.json` gate is default-on first because it is CRITICAL command execution and needs only a notice. The rules, agents, overlay and plugins gate ships in the same push as the TTY prompt, so interactive users are asked rather than silently degraded. The operator-env filter lands after cluster A's autoload flags. There is no env kill switch because env is repo-forgeable. The escape hatches are the explicit grant channels: prompt, `quanta trust`, real-env QUANTA_TRUSTED_PATHS, and optionally --trust-project.
revisedDesign.costEstimate: BUG-1 lane: about 11 src plus 6 test files, roughly 450-600 LOC including tests (S-M). SEC-5 S1-S3 (decision module, MCP gate, operator env): about 7 src plus 4 test files, roughly 500 LOC (S-M). S4-S7 (bootstrap wiring, prompt, siblings, dedupe, test migrations): about 16 src plus 14 test files, roughly 900-1,200 LOC (M-L). Build flags are cluster A's (S).

userDecisions.question: Who lands the Bun compile autoload flags (--no-compile-autoload-dotenv/--no-compile-autoload-bunfig) and the `.mcp.json` trust gate?
userDecisions.options: (a) Cluster A owns the build flags; D owns the MCP gate via the shared ProjectTrustDecision. (b) D lands both. (c) An exec/MCP cluster owns the MCP gate and consumes D's resolveProjectTrust.
userDecisions.recommendation: (a). A is already probing bunfig/dotenv hardening (wf/A-r1/bunprobe). One trust decision SSOT means the MCP gate should use D's module, whoever types it.

userDecisions.question: Interactive TTY, untrusted folder with repo-authority artifacts: what happens?
userDecisions.options: (a) One-time prompt; decline continues without the artifacts. (b) Prompt; decline exits (CC 'No, exit', chunk-03ah04wm.js:526-545). (c) Notice only.
userDecisions.recommendation: (a): asks once, never blocks work, and the decline is visible in /rules and /status.

userDecisions.question: Default for non-interactive surfaces (`quanta -p`, CI, serve --stdio, SDK)
userDecisions.options: (a) Untrusted unless an operator grant (Codex exec: 'Not inside a trusted directory...', _cli-symbols.txt:21457). (b) Implicitly trusted like CC -p (chunk-m04a62n5.js:27866-27869).
userDecisions.recommendation: (a). Bench/eval surfaces do not depend on repo rules (verified), so the cost falls on users running `quanta -p` in their own CI, who get a one-line notice naming the grant channels.

userDecisions.question: Grant channel for headless/CI
userDecisions.options: (a) Real-env QUANTA_TRUSTED_PATHS only (valid once A's autoload flag lands). (b) Add a `--trust-project` argv flag (session-only, not persisted; argv is not repo-forgeable). (c) `quanta trust <path>` as a pre-step writing trust.json.
userDecisions.recommendation: (b) plus (c), keeping (a) for compatibility. Argv is the one channel a repo file cannot forge even in source-mode runs.

userDecisions.question: Scope of the trust gate
userDecisions.options: (a) Instruction files only. (b) All repo-authority artifacts through one decision: AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, .mcp.json, .quanta/agents and .claude/agents, .quanta/project-grants.json, .quanta/plugins, vendor/glob rules, legacy settings.json hooks.

userDecisions.question: Trust granularity
userDecisions.options: (a) Realpath git root; nested repos need their own trust; loose dirs keyed at the exact cwd. (b) CC-style ancestor inheritance inside the git root (chunk-m04a62n5.js:28040-28049). (c) Exact cwd only.
userDecisions.recommendation: (a). One key, one walk bound, and no ancestor record silently covering an unrelated subtree.

userDecisions.question: Web/Tauri trust UX
userDecisions.options: (a) Readout banner plus a 'Trust folder' action (the daemon writes TrustStore; takes effect in a new session). (b) Native dialog at folder open. (c) Launch flag only.

userDecisions.question: IDE (serve --stdio) trust source
userDecisions.options: (a) TrustStore/operator grant only. (b) A host-attested workspace-trust bit in the session.v1 handshake.
userDecisions.recommendation: (a) now; (b) as a later protocol field.

userDecisions.question: Home directory grants
userDecisions.options: (a) Session-only, never persisted (CC CHANGELOG-upstream.md:1618 per R1). (b) Persist like any folder.

userDecisions.question: Authority rank of TRUSTED repo rules vs the user request (prompt-body.ts:36-46 ranks L6 above L8)
userDecisions.options: (a) The user request overrides repo rules except L1-L5 (Cursor main.js:58377-58379). (b) Keep repo rules above the user.

userDecisions.question: Protect trust.json and grants.json from model writes
userDecisions.options: (a) Hard-deny bash/write/edit on the quanta home trust files (separate small change). (b) Leave as is.
userDecisions.recommendation: (a), as its own change; otherwise the model can self-grant.

residualRisks: TypeScript deep identity and assignability are order- and depth-limited (probe-guard-forms*.ts), so the only completeness proof for Message fidelity is runtime (B-T1/B-T2). Top-level SavedSession subtrees (objective, rollback, meta) keep their existing per-RFC tests and get no Complete<> fixture in this plan.

Source-mode runs (`bun run src/apps/cli/index.ts`) still autoload a cwd bunfig.toml and .env unless started with --no-env-file; the flag does not stop bunfig (my probe: marker 1 with --no-env-file). Only the compiled binary is hardened by A's flags, so dev launch scripts are cluster A's residual.
The operator-env view is complete only once A's flags ship. If D's S3 lands first it must not claim forge resistance.

A brand-new reader of a repo-authority artifact that neither uses TrustedProjectRoot nor registers in REPO_AUTHORITY_ARTIFACTS is not caught mechanically, because 'authority' vs 'data' is semantic. The dropped constant-reference census would have been evadable anyway.

MESSAGE_RAILS is a hand list; its completeness rests on the single-decode chokepoint pin (one savedSessionSchema.safeParse) plus V1/ipc using firstInvalidMessageElement. A future rail with its own decoder needs its own entry.
Dotenv relocation of the skill dirs (D-H6) and dotenv-set feature gates (QUANTA_MIGRATE_CONFIG*, QUANTA_LLM_CREDENTIAL_TRUSTED) stay open until cluster A decides what a cwd dotenv may set.
Plugin spawn via mention (D-H9) was not driven end to end.
The waitingOn narrowing was typechecked only over 238 reachable files, not the whole repo.
Model self-grant by writing ~/.quanta/trust.json stays possible until the protected-path change lands.
The TOCTOU between the listed artifacts at grant time and later content matches CC and Codex behavior (they trust the folder, not a content digest).
Resume-then-save stripping through the real REPL loop is inferred from the store-level probes and was not driven through a pty session.
